chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may Allah have mercy on them both) said: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, and Ahmad ibn Idris both narrated, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from some of our companions, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Tahi, from Tahir ibn Hatim ibn Mahawayh, who said: I wrote to al-Tayyib - meaning Abu al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him): 'What is that without which the recognition of the Creator is not valid?' So he wrote back: 'There is nothing whatsoever like unto Him, and He has always been All-Hearing, All-Knowing, and All-Seeing, and He is the Doer of what He wills.'

key_terms.لَيْسَ كَمِثْلِهِ شَيْءٌ: There is nothing like unto Him (Quranic phrase denoting divine uniqueness)

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum requirement for recognizing God according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) identifies the core of Tawhid as the negation of likeness (La Mithl), derived from Surah Ash-Shura, establishing that God’s essence is entirely distinct from creation. This response underscores that true recognition of the Creator requires affirming His absolute sovereignty ('He is the Doer of what He wills') alongside His perfect attributes of Hearing, Knowing, and Seeing, ensuring believers avoid both anthropomorphism and total negation.
